# Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold

## Problem statement

When the herdr worklist selection list (`createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) has more work items than fit in the visible list area, the renderer silently trims the visible window to fit the pane height. There is no visual cue (scroll marker, count, ellipsis) that additional items exist below the fold, so users cannot tell the list is truncated and may miss items.

## Users

Anyone using the herdr worklist pane (`worklog-selection-list` plug) to browse/select work items, in particular with more items than fit on screen (the default list of 20+ items on smaller panes, or with the metadata panel reserving 20–40% of the height).

User story: *"As a herdr user, when the worklist pane shows more items than fit, I want to see a `▼ more` marker so I know the list continues below the fold and I can scroll (j/k) to see the rest."*

User story: *"As a herdr user who has scrolled down, I want to see an `▲ more` marker at the top of the list so I know there are items above the current viewport."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the flattened item list exceeds the visible list area at scroll offset 0, the rendered list output contains a dim-styled `▼ more` marker at the bottom of the items region (after the last visible item, before the footer/fill rows).
- When the list is scrolled down (scrollOffset > 0) with items above the viewport, the rendered output contains a dim-styled `▲ more` marker at the top of the items region (before the first visible item/group separator).
- When all items fit in the visible area (no overflow, scrollOffset = 0), no indicators are rendered.
- The `rows - 1` line-count invariant is preserved with indicators active: rendered output plus the notification line still fits the pane height (regression guard for WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).
- Indicators are non-selectable display-only rows: they do not consume navigation state, selection index, or hierarchy scroll offset (`getVisibleItems`, `_adjustScroll` semantics unchanged).
- New unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: indicator shown when items exist below the fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when the list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Must preserve the `rows - 1` line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO (notification line always fits; header never scrolls off the top).
- Indicator wording is generic ("more"), not exact counts — group separator rows make exact "N more" counts unreliable.
- Scope is list mode only: the detail view and the metadata panel (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X) are unchanged.
- Match existing styling conventions: dim-styled (`ANSI.dim`), consistent with other non-interactive chrome (footer hints, filter bar).
- Indicator rows must be included in the render budget (the `visible` trimming loop and the fill-blank count) so output never exceeds the pane.

## Existing state

- `createListRenderer` sizes the visible window with `flatItems.slice(scrollOffset, scrollOffset + listHeight)` and trims it with `visible.slice(0, -1)` when items + group separators exceed `budgetForItemsAndSeps`. Nothing signals that trimming happened.
- The pane header shows `(top N of M)` only when the *fetch* was truncated (`totalCount > items.length`), not when the *display* is truncated by the viewport — so a full fetch with a small pane shows no cue at all.
- Scrolling works (j/k via `scrollOffset`, `_adjustScroll` keeps the selection visible), but at rest positions there is no indication of hidden items in either direction.
- The Pi TUI browse list (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) is a separate surface and already shows `(top N of M)` in its title; pi's built-in `SelectList` component renders a `(N/M)` scroll-info line when overflow exists — the established pattern this change mirrors.

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer` (list mode), after the visible window is trimmed to fit:
  - Emit a dim `▼ more` line at the bottom of the items region when `scrollOffset + visible.length < flatItems.length` (items below the fold).
  - Emit a dim `▲ more` line at the top of the items region when `scrollOffset > 0` (items above the viewport).
  - Account for indicator rows in the budget: include them in the trimming calculation and in the fill-blank `used` count so the `rows - 1` invariant holds.
  - Edge case: if reserving the bottom indicator row trims the window so that `scrollOffset + visible.length == flatItems.length`, the bottom indicator is omitted (the list then fully fits); this must terminate in a single pass (no loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer`: compute indicator presence from `scrollOffset`/the trimmed visible window, emit `▼ more`/`▲ more` rows, and include them in the budget (`budgetForItemsAndSeps` trimming loop + fill-blank `used` count).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — add unit tests: indicator shown when items below fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active; indicators are non-selectable display rows.

## Related work

- [Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO)] — completed; established the `rows - 1` line-count invariant and the visible-window trimming logic this change extends.
- [Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)] — completed; defines `listArea`/`panelHeight`, the fold boundary of the list region.
- [Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)] — origin of the selection list.
- pi-tui `SelectList` component (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/components/select-list.js`) — reference pattern: `(N/M)` scroll-info line when the list overflows `maxVisible`.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: generic "more" wording is sufficient (user: "more" is fine); exact counts are intentionally avoided because group separators make them unreliable.
- Risk: indicator rows shrink the visible item window by up to 2 rows when overflow exists. Acceptable — the alternative (no indicator) is the bug being fixed.
- Risk: budget accounting bugs could regress the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO line-count invariant. Mitigation: the existing invariant tests plus new tests with indicators active cover both top and bottom indicators.
- Edge case: bottom indicator row reservation could trim the window to fully fit, making the indicator unnecessary — handle without looping.
- Scope-creep guard: the Pi TUI browse list also lacks a fold indicator, but it already shows `(top N of M)`; improving that surface is out of scope and could be tracked as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Indicator style — which do you prefer? (a) a footer line in the items region like `▼ N more` (dim), shown when items exist below the fold; (b) a position indicator like `(N/M)`; (c) both: `▼ N more` footer plus a `▲ N more` header when scrolled down" — Answer (user): "(c) Both". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope — should this cover only the list-mode pane (herdr worklist), or also the detail-view scroll indicator (which already exists via the metadata panel scroll)?" — Answer (user): "confirm" (list-mode only). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Count precision — exact remaining count (e.g. `▼ 5 more`) vs. a generic marker (e.g. `▼ more`)? Exact counts can be wrong when group separators consume rows." — Answer (user): "`more` is fine". Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MP15YJEQ000FVWS** – Documentation: colour mapping & fallbacks (completed)
- **WL-0MLRFF0771A8NAVW** – TUI: prevent mouse click-through from dialogs to underlying widgets (completed)
- **WL-0MLOS7X1C1P82B5J** – Append no-questions instruction to OpenCode prompt (completed)

# Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen

## Problem statement

In the Herdr plugin's work-item detail view, when an item has a `Related Docs` Table of Contents (ToC) (i.e. ≥1 `.md` Key File), the rendered output exceeds the pane height: the header (id/title) and the first ToC lines scroll off the top of the screen, so the ToC is not entirely visible. The ToC is also rendered twice and the item header is dropped entirely.

## Users

- **Herdr users** viewing a work item's detail view in the plugin pane, who need the item header and the full `Related Docs` ToC visible at the top of the pane while the metadata/description/document body scrolls beneath.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the item id, title, and the complete Related Docs ToC when I open a work item's detail view, so nothing important is cut off at the top of the screen.
- As a Herdr user, I want the ToC to stay pinned while I scroll the document, so I can always see which documents are linked to the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an item has a ToC (≥1 `.md` Key File), the detail view shows the header (id, title, separator) and the **full** ToC at the top of the pane at scroll 0 — no lines cut off. The ToC is rendered **exactly once** (no duplication), and the item header is present.
2. Detail-view output never exceeds the pane: `formatDetailView` returns at most `viewportHeight` lines, and the full renderer (`createListRenderer` detail mode) returns at most `rows - 1` lines — the line-count invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO holds for detail mode with a ToC present.
3. The header + ToC block stays **pinned** at the top while the body (metadata table, description, md viewer) scrolls beneath it; scrolling is limited to the body region (viewport height minus the pinned block height), and `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamps against the same reduced body viewport. No dead/blank region at the bottom when fully scrolled.
4. Items **without** `.md` Key Files (no ToC) keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (regression check — no behavior change for the no-ToC path).
5. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: line-count invariant for detail mode with ToC (renderer ≤ `rows - 1`; `formatDetailView` ≤ `viewportHeight`), header + ToC fully visible at scroll 0, ToC not duplicated, pinned-ToC scroll regression (existing `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` test kept green/updated), and no-ToC behavior unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the detail-view ToC layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Preserve the pinned-ToC design from WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29: the ToC stays visible on all renders; only the body below it scrolls.
- Respect the line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO: the renderer must never emit more than `rows - 1` lines, otherwise the terminal scrolls the top of the output off the pane.
- Surgical change: do not alter scrolling behavior for items without a ToC (the pre-existing full-scroll path).
- No new dependencies; reuse the existing `formatDetailToC` / `formatDetailContent` helpers.

## Existing state

- `formatDetailView` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, ~line 1223) builds the detail output as `[...tocLines, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + viewportHeight)]` where `bodyLines = allLines.slice(tocLines.length)`.
- The slicing assumes the ToC occupies the first `tocLines.length` lines of `allLines`, but `formatDetailContent` emits the header first (blank, id, title, separator = 4 lines) and the ToC **after** it. Consequences (verified by reproduction): (a) the header is dropped from the output, (b) the ToC is duplicated (once from `tocLines`, once inside `bodyLines`), (c) total output = `viewportHeight + tocLines.length` lines, which overflows the pane (`viewportHeight = rows - 1` in the renderer). Reproduction: `formatDetailView(item, 80, 0, 20)` with a 2-entry ToC returns 26 lines; the renderer on a 24-row terminal emits 29 lines (max allowed 23).
- Regression introduced in commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I, "Implementation complete").
- `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` (~line 496) computes `maxScroll` against the full `viewportHeight` instead of the body region, so clamping is also wrong for the pinned layout.
- The existing test `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` only asserts the ToC appears in the first 8 lines — it never checks the total line count, so it passes despite the overflow.

## Desired change

1. In `formatDetailView`, compute a **pinned block** = header (4 lines: blank, id, title, separator) + `tocLines`; the scrollable **body** = `allLines.slice(pinnedHeight)`; the **body viewport** = `max(1, viewportHeight - pinnedHeight)`; `maxScroll = max(0, bodyLines.length - bodyViewport)`. Render `[...pinned, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + bodyViewport)]` and update the scroll-indicator percentage math to use `bodyViewport`.
2. Keep the no-ToC path (`tocLines.length === 0`) identical to the pre-ToC behavior (whole content scrolls, header included) to avoid scope creep.
3. Update `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` to clamp against the reduced body viewport (subtract the pinned height) so `j`/`G` behave consistently with the renderer.
4. Optionally introduce a named constant (e.g. `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES = 4`) documenting the fixed header shape so the slicing is self-explanatory.
5. Add/extend unit tests per AC5; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it describes the detail-view layout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailView` pinned header+ToC slicing and body-viewport math; `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamp; optional header-lines constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — line-count invariant tests for detail mode with ToC, header/ToC visibility at scroll 0, no-duplication check, no-ToC regression, updated pinned-ToC test.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the pinned header + ToC detail-view layout if it describes the ToC behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Header-shape fragility:** the fix relies on the header being exactly 4 lines (blank, id, title, separator). Mitigate by introducing a named `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES` constant next to `formatDetailContent` and by an AC1 test asserting the header is visible at scroll 0.
- **No-ToC regression:** altering `formatDetailView` slicing could accidentally change the full-scroll path for items without `.md` Key Files. Mitigate with AC4 regression test asserting the no-ToC path is unchanged.
- **Viewport-height mismatch:** the state class uses `rows - 4` while the renderer uses `rows - 1`; today the renderer's clamp absorbs the difference. The fix must subtract the pinned height consistently in both `formatDetailView` and `detailScrollDown` so `j`/`G` and the on-screen clamp agree.
- **Scope creep:** pinning the header for ALL items (even without a ToC) is deliberately out of scope — it is a UX change beyond the reported bug. Recorded as an assumption; can be tracked as a separate work item if desired.
- **Assumption:** the fix pins header + ToC together (the header sits above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC keeps the header visible) and scrolls only the body (metadata/description/md viewer) beneath — faithful to the pinned-ToC design intent (WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3) and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I` (completed) — "Herdr: detail-view ToC for Related Docs (arrow/j/k navigate, Enter renders)" — the pinned-ToC implementation that introduced this regression (commit `76a52c9f`).
- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` (completed) — "Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer)" — defines the pinned-ToC design intent.
- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` (completed) — "Herdr: pane line-count invariant (rows - 1)" — the invariant the detail view now violates.
- `WL-0MS31WX9C008FIQR` (completed) — "Full scrollable detail view" — original detail-view scrolling design (whole content scrolls).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required for this intake.

- The seed report ("The table of contents on the detail view of work items is not entirely visible — the first few lines are off the top of the screen") combined with repository analysis was conclusive: the root cause was located by inspection of `formatDetailView`/`formatDetailContent` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, confirmed by a reproduction test (26 lines emitted for a 20-line viewport; 29 lines for a 24-row terminal vs. the 23-line invariant), and pinned to the regression commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I) via `git log -S`.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): the fix pins the **header + ToC** block at the top of the detail view (the header is above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC necessarily keeps the header visible) while the body scrolls beneath — this is the faithful reading of the pinned-ToC design intent in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3 ("The ToC stays visible on all renders") and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): items **without** `.md` Key Files keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (surgical scope).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKXJPCDI1FLYDB1** – Prompt input box must resize on word wrap (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4WX0073W30** – Arbitrary-depth chords in detail view (completed)
- **WL-0MQQW534Q009JSX7** – Remove superfluous ## Stage section from wl create output (completed)

## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, every fetch used by the auto-refresh cycle spawns `wl` via execFile WITHOUT a timeout: `runWl(args)` (fetcher.ts:376) passes `timeout` to execFileAsync only when `timeoutMs !== undefined` (:356), and no caller in the refresh path supplies one (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount). `doRefresh` awaits these inside a `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts:2497-2503); if a spawn hangs (e.g. waiting on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child), the guard stays true forever and EVERY subsequent refresh is skipped — the pane freezes even while focused, with no error surfaced.

Note: runSync (auto-sync.ts:226) already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; the refresh read path does not.

related-to: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (same bug class in the downtime worker path — getNextItem/getNextAuditCandidate in index.ts use direct execFileAsync with no timeout; a single fix adding bounded timeouts to ALL wl spawns would close both).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every wl spawn in the refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout (recommend 30-60s, configurable or aligned with existing constants).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: toast (`Refresh failed`), guard cleared, next tick retries — never a permanently wedged refreshInFlight.
- [ ] Unit tests: hung execFile resolves to failure after the timeout and the next refresh tick proceeds.

## Suggested approach

Pass a default timeoutMs inside runWl (or runWlInner) when the caller omits one, e.g. `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, keeping the option to override. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns.

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Plan

### Child Work Items (dependency-ordered)

1. **WL-0MT5L3BGA001MKOP** - Create pickFields() projection helper module
2. **WL-0MT5L4MGL000Z43Y** - Write unit tests for pickFields projection helper (depends on 1)
3. **WL-0MT5L55AQ002WTGQ** - Add --fields option to wl list (depends on 1, 2)
4. **WL-0MT5L6G88006N4WD** - Add --fields option to wl search (depends on 1, 2)
5. **WL-0MT5L6TLQ004NDLK** - Integration test: end-to-end --fields flag verification (depends on 3, 4)

### Implementation Approach

1. Create packages/shared/src/fields.ts with pickFields(item, fields?) helper
2. Add fields?: string to ListOptions and SearchOptions in cli-types.ts
3. Apply pickFields projection in list.ts before JSON output
4. Apply pickFields projection in search.ts before JSON output
5. Write unit tests and integration tests

### Review Stages Summary

1. Requirements & AC alignment: All 5 ACs map to user stories and expected behaviour. No gaps or contradictions.
2. Completeness: Description has all required sections. Key files are valid.
3. Sequencing & dependencies: Test items before implementation items. Dependencies properly set.
4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.
5. Acceptance & testability: All ACs are testable with clear pass/fail criteria.
6. Polish & handoff: Plan is copy-pasteable and actionable.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

## Appendix

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.

# Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (cheap on operator idle, fast on operator command)

## Problem statement

The llama-proxy runs in two operating modes — **fast** (cloud-backed, 3-slot pool) and **cheap** (2-slot local-first pool). Today mode is switched manually (admin API/UI) or on a fixed time schedule; there is no link between *operator presence* and mode. When an operator is actively working through the herdr plugin, every Pi command should be served by **fast** mode; when the operator leaves (no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for a configurable window), the proxy should drop to **cheap** mode so the downtime worker's autonomous dispatches consume only the cheap local pool.

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** — wants fast responses while actively working and zero-cost cheap mode when away, without touching the mode API by hand.

Example user stories:

- *"As an operator, when I issue an agent command (/skill:*, /intake, /plan, /prompt:) through the herdr plugin, I want the proxy switched to fast mode immediately so my session is served by the cloud-backed pool."*
- *"As an operator, when I have issued no agent-route Pi commands through the plugin for 15 minutes, I want the proxy switched to cheap mode (only when it is idle) so the downtime dispatcher's work runs on the cheap local pool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Operator-activity tracking:** the plugin records a timestamp on every **agent-route** command (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` — the routes that spawn a pi agent pane); shell shortcuts (`!!`/`!`) and plain commands do NOT count as operator activity.
- [ ] **Cheap switch on idle:** when no operator agent-route command has been routed for ≥ `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` (default `900000` = 15 min, configurable) **AND** the proxy reports idle (reusing the existing `/llama/local/status` idle evaluation: llama-server running, no active local query, no model switch, no local lease, all required slots free), the worker POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}`. A busy proxy (active local query) **delays** the switch (never kills in-flight work).
- [ ] **Fast switch on command:** when a new operator agent-route command is routed through the plugin, it immediately POSTs `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}` (fire-and-forget; a failed switch never blocks or delays the command dispatch — the pane opens regardless, fail-open).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** the worker skips a switch when the persisted mode already matches the target (track last-known mode; refresh via `GET /admin/mode` on poll). At most one switch per state change; a `409` (mode-switch restart in progress) is treated as a no-op and retried on a later tick.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, network errors, and ambiguous responses yield no switch and never crash or block the plugin. On plugin restart the idle clock resets to "active now" (fail-safe: the proxy stays fast until a fresh full idle window passes).
- [ ] **Configurable via plugin settings** (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`): enabled toggle, idle threshold ms, poll interval ms; settings re-read every tick so changes apply without a plugin restart. The proxy URL is shared with the downtime worker (`downtimeProxyUrl`).
- [ ] **Coexistence with the proxy's built-in schedule:** the plugin's switches are manual overrides (the API's native semantics, LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J); the proxy's time-based schedule (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00) reclaims control at its next boundary. Documented behavior, not a conflict.
- [ ] **Testing & validation:** unit tests cover idle-window evaluation, last-command tracking, cheap/fast switch triggers, restart reset, fail-closed paths, and settings clamps. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the herdr README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only **agent-route** commands count as operator activity (operator decision Q1).
- The cheap switch is gated on proxy idle — it must never kill in-flight work (operator decision Q4b).
- Mode switches never block the TUI or command dispatch: all HTTP calls are fire-and-forget (fast switch) or scheduled task work (cheap switch).
- Fail-closed at every boundary: no crash, no hammering, no repeated identical POSTs.
- The seed mentions "the `/admin/mode` API": `GET /admin/mode` only *reads* the mode; the switch endpoint is `POST /admin/set-mode`. The brief targets `/admin/set-mode`.

## Existing state

- Mode API + UI exist on the proxy: `GET /admin/mode`, `POST /admin/set-mode` (LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6); mode persisted in `proxy/.mode`, defaults to `fast`.
- Time-based automatic mode switching exists on the proxy (cheap 01:00–10:00, fast 10:00–01:00, LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX) with manual-override persistence until the next scheduled change (LP-0MSMF25V9002AY1J). A mode switch restarts the proxy (terminates in-flight requests; clients retry — documented accepted behavior).
- The herdr plugin already has: settings system (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`, re-read per tick), a consolidated scheduler (worklist.ts), and a downtime worker that polls `/llama/local/status` with fail-closed idle evaluation (WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K + children). The mode-switch worker reuses this infrastructure.

## Desired change

Add a mode-switch worker to the herdr plugin:

1. `index.ts` `onCommand` (agent route) records `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` and fires the fast switch (`POST /admin/set-mode {"mode":"fast"}`, fire-and-forget, fail-open).
2. A new scheduler task (pattern-matched on the existing `downtime` task) ticks on `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs`: if `lastOperatorCommandAt` is null/older than the threshold AND the proxy is idle (reuse the local-status poller/idle evaluation), POST `/admin/set-mode {"mode":"cheap"}` — skipping when the persisted mode already is cheap.
3. New settings: `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs`, `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` (reusing `downtimeProxyUrl`); re-read each tick.
4. Restart behavior: worker construction sets `lastOperatorCommandAt = Date.now()` (reset to active).

- **WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K** — "Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime" (parent of the downtime worker; the poller/settings/scheduler infrastructure this feature reuses)
- **LP-0MSLMYEEU002IBH6** (llm-manager) — Web API/UI to toggle fast/cheap modes (the `/admin/mode` + `/admin/set-mode` endpoints)
- **LP-0MSM5K4TX004MICX** (llm-manager) — Time-based automatic mode switching (built-in schedule)

- **Mode switch restarts the proxy** (kills in-flight requests). Mitigated for the cheap direction by the idle gate (Q4b); the fast direction can still kill a cheap-mode downtime request when the operator returns — accepted (documented proxy behavior; the downtime dispatch's work retries on the next idle period).
- **Multiple plugin panes** could each run a mode-switch worker → duplicate POSTs. Same-mode POSTs are API noops and the worker skips already-matching modes, so the system converges; per-process single-flight is applied.
- **Schedule reassertion at boundaries** may flip the mode shortly after a plugin switch near a boundary — accepted; every new operator command re-switches to fast immediately (design intent).
- **`GET /admin/mode`/`POST /admin/set-mode` may not be reachable** from the plugin host — fail-closed (no switch), never crash; the plugin logs a warning.
- **Scope-creep risk:** related but out-of-scope opportunities (e.g., reflecting the active mode in the herdr UI, per-slot idle gating for the cheap switch, or activity-based mode tracking for non-plugin pi panes) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.

# Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)

## Headline

Flip the space priority in the Herdr worklist pane: the selection list may use up to the full available pane height (including its header lines), and the metadata section fills whatever space remains — expanding when the list is short, sitting below the fold (revealed by scrolling down) when the list is long — scrolling internally when its content overflows.

## Problem statement

The metadata section below the selection list currently reserves a fixed 20–40% of the pane height (`computeMetadataPanelHeight`), squeezing the list. When the list needs more vertical space than it is allotted, it scrolls and the header/top lines scroll off the top of the pane, even though the metadata section below is eating rows the list could use. The metadata section should no longer force the list to scroll off the top.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selection list — including its header line — to use as much vertical space as it needs, up to the maximum available, so items don't scroll off the top prematurely.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when the list is long, I want the list (header + items) to take up to the full pane height so I can see as many items as possible without the top scrolling off.
- As a Herdr user, when the list is short, I want the metadata section to expand into the leftover space so the pane still shows the selected item's metadata.
- As a Herdr user, when the list fills the full pane, I want to scroll the pane down to expose the rest of the list and then the metadata section, with the initial view starting at the top of the selection list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List takes as much space as it needs, up to the max available**: The selection list (header line + items + group separators + footer) can use up to the maximum number of vertical lines available in the pane (pane rows minus the reserved notification row). The metadata section no longer reserves a fixed 20–40% share that forces the list to scroll.
2. **Initial view at top**: When the list fills the full vertical space, the view starts at the top of the selection list (header + first items visible). Scrolling the pane down exposes the rest of the list and, at the end, the metadata section.
3. **Metadata fills the rest**: When the list content is shorter than the available height, the metadata section expands to fill the leftover space below the list.
4. **Metadata scrolls if necessary**: When the metadata content overflows the space allotted to it, it scrolls independently using the existing `m`/`M` keys and `metaScrollOffset` (with the existing `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator), and the selection-driven reset behaviour is preserved.
5. **No regression**: Keyboard navigation (arrows/j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap), stage filtering, group separators, auto-refresh, code-freeze banner, and the reserved notification row continue to work; rendered output never exceeds the pane's `rows` budget.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests cover (a) list height = min(content need, max available), (b) metadata expansion when the list is short, (c) reveal-by-scroll when the list fills the pane and initial view at top, (d) metadata scroll clamping under the new layout, and (e) the output line-count invariant (≤ `rows`).
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Plugin-local change in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; no `wl` CLI or backend schema changes.
- The rendered output must never exceed the pane's `rows` budget (last row reserved for the notification line; group-separator accounting must not overflow) — the invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO must hold.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings: `m`/`M` for metadata scrolling, and all list-navigation keys unchanged.
- Must compose with the description preview feature (WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3, in progress) which adds up to 3 preview lines to the metadata panel content.
- The metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) whenever it is rendered (short list or scrolled into view) so it remains usable, even if that means its content scrolls internally.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — document-flow layout**: the user's answers describe the list and metadata section as stacked content within one scrollable viewport (view starts at top; scrolling down reveals the rest of the list, then the metadata). An alternative pinned-footer layout (metadata always visible at the pane bottom) does not match the answers and is out of scope.
- **Assumption — header behavior**: "start the view at the top of the selection list" is interpreted as the initial render showing header + first items; the exact pin-vs-scroll behaviour of the header line during scroll is an implementation detail, but the header must be visible initially (matching the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO invariant that the header is never cut off).
- **Risk — line-count regression**: changing the list/metadata space split could reintroduce output overflowing the pane (the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO bug). Mitigation: keep the ≤ `rows` invariant as an explicit test.
- **Risk — metadata scroll clamping**: if the panel's allotted height changes dynamically, `metaScrollDown`'s clamp against content height must still hold; keep the existing clamp tests and update them for the new sizing.
- **Risk — scope creep**: "below the fold" indicators (WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ), mouse/touch scrolling (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ), and metadata panel content changes (WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7) are related but separate items — do not implement them here.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)` (lines ~85–119) — reserves a 20–40% share of pane rows for the metadata panel (min 3 rows), from WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X.
  - `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` (line ~681) — `max(3, rows - 4 - panelHeight)`; used by `_adjustScroll` and `getVisibleItems`.
  - `createListRenderer()` (line ~1830) — computes `panelHeight = computeMetadataPanelHeight(rows)`, `listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`, `listHeight = rows - 4 - panelHeight`; renders header + items + separators + fill + footer + metadata panel lines, clamped to `rows - 1`.
  - `formatMetadataPanel()` (line ~982) — renders exactly `panelRows` lines with independent scroll offset and `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator; `metaScrollDown` clamps against content height.
  - `metaScrollOffset` reset on selection change (`_resetMetaScroll`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `computeMetadataPanelHeight` responsive-ramp tests (lines ~1448), metadata scroll clamp tests (line ~1663), renderer line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — entry point wiring (render callback passes `metaScrollOffset`/`metaLastCommand`).

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer()`: compute the list's space need from its content (header + banner + items + separators + footer), capped at the maximum available rows (`rows - 1` minus the notification budget). The metadata section is allotted the remainder: it expands to fill leftover space when the list is short, and when the list fills the pane it is positioned below the list content so scrolling down reveals the rest of the list and then the metadata section.
- Initial view starts at the top of the selection list (scroll offset 0 / header visible) even when the list is long.
- Keep `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (or replace its call sites) such that the fixed 20–40% reservation no longer forces the list to scroll; the metadata panel keeps a small minimum height (~3 rows) and scrolls internally via `metaScrollOffset`/`m`/`M` when its content overflows.
- Keep `formatMetadataPanel`'s independent-scroll contract (exactly `panelRows` lines) and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — list/metadata space split, initial view-at-top, metadata scroll clamping; primary change location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — update responsive-ramp tests; add list-height/content-need, metadata-expansion, reveal-by-scroll, and line-count invariant tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — render callback wiring (`metaScrollOffset`, `metaLastCommand`), only if the space split needs state/context passed through.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** (completed) — introduced the metadata panel and the fixed 20–40% reservation this item reverses; its AC1 said the list "always keeps the majority of the space (≥60%)" — this item changes that priority.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** (in progress) — adds a description preview to the metadata panel (up to 3 lines), which makes the metadata content taller; this item must compose with it.
- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** (completed) — the output line-count invariant (`≤ rows`) this item must preserve.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** (open) — "no indication of items below the fold" — related scrolling UX; not required by this item but related.
- **WL-0MSHIJR7T007Q9R7** (open) — drops the duplicate ID row from the metadata panel; touches the same `formatMetadataPanel` output.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When the list is long and fills the pane, should the metadata panel keep a small guaranteed minimum (e.g., ~3 rows, as today) so it stays visible and scrolls within that, or may it shrink all the way to zero (hidden)?" — Answer (user): "If the selection list takes up the full vertical space scrolling the pane down should expose the rest of the list and the meta-data section. However we should start the view at the top of the selection list." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: when the list fills the pane, the metadata section sits below the list content and is revealed by scrolling the pane down; the initial view starts at the top of the selection list (header visible). Research: inspected `computeMetadataPanelHeight` (20–40% fixed reservation) and the renderer's `listArea`/`listHeight` budget in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- Q2: "When the list has only a few items, should the list take only the rows it needs (header + items + separators + footer) and let the metadata panel expand to fill the leftover space, or should the list always occupy the full available height and the metadata panel stay at a fixed small size?" — Answer (user): "meta-data can expand to fill space." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the list takes only what it needs when short; the metadata section expands into the leftover space.
- Q3: "Should the existing m/M metadata scrolling behavior stay as-is, just operating in the new (possibly smaller) panel space?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. Research: `metaScrollOffset`, `_resetMetaScroll` on selection change, `metaScrollUp/Down` clamping and the `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator already exist in `worklist.ts`.

# Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file

## Problem statement

The current Downtime Dispatcher has every herdr plugin instance polling the llama-proxy independently, using priority, round-robin, and jitter to share dispatch load. This approach still allows one instance to dominate dispatches and doesn't scale well when many instances are active. A leader-election model with a shared coordination file would simplify the dispatch logic: all instances contribute their most important work item to a shared list, one elected leader dispatches work from that list, and the coordination file acts as the single source of truth.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants fair dispatch distribution without per-instance polling complexity; each instance contributes its worklog's most important item to a shared queue.
- **Operator with idle local LLM** — wants work dispatched efficiently: the leader polls for idle slots and pulls from the coordination list, removing dispatched items so others can re-queue.

### User stories

- As an operator running N herdr instances, each instance should automatically join a shared coordination list with its most important work item from its own worklog, identified by instance and worklog directory.
- As an operator, I want one elected leader to handle all LLM idle checks and dispatches, so the other instances don't waste cycles polling the proxy.
- As an operator, if the leader crashes, another instance should automatically take over within 5 minutes.
- As an operator, when the leader dispatches an item, that item is removed from the coordination list and the instance that owned it will add a new item on its next 30-minute check-in.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Leader election** — Instances use a file lock to elect a single leader; the first instance to acquire the lock wins. If no leader is elected (lock unavailable), the instance continues operating without dispatching.
2. **Lease-based leadership** — The leader holds a 5-minute lease, refreshed every time it polls the llama-proxy. If the lease expires (leader crashed or idle), instances detect the expiry and run a new election.
3. **Coordination file** — A shared JSON file at `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` stores one entry per instance: `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`. Each instance:
   - On startup and every 30 minutes, reads the coordination file
   - If it has an entry, verifies its work item is still its most important; if not, updates the entry
   - If no entry exists, adds its most important item to the list
   - If its entry was removed (by leader dispatch), adds a new entry on the next check-in
4. **Leader dispatch logic** — The leader reads the coordination file, determines priority order (audit tier first, then implement, then plan, then intake), checks LLM idle status (same 30s proxy poll + 4 min continuous idle threshold), and dispatches the highest-priority available item when a slot opens. The dispatched item is removed from the coordination file.
5. **Multi-worklog support** — Each instance operates on its own worklog directory (identified in the coordination file). The leader compares work items across directories using the standard tier priority system.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Single-machine only for v1** — coordination file access uses flock; no cross-machine support in this version.
- **30-minute check-in interval** — instances update the coordination file every 30 minutes (first check-in on startup).
- **5-minute lease** — leader lease timeout is 5 minutes, refreshed on each proxy poll cycle.
- **Fail-safe** — missing/unreadable coordination file or failed leader election degrades to current behavior (no dispatch from that instance).
- **Existing dispatch guard preserved** — the dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim mechanisms continue to prevent double-dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` runs tiers in order: audit → implement → plan → intake.
- Each herdr instance polls the llama-proxy independently using fixed jittered intervals.
- Dispatch markers (`downtime-dispatches.log`) + CAS claim prevent double-dispatch.
- Coordination file concept doesn't exist; all state is instance-local.
- Key files: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Leader election module** — New file (`leader-election.ts`) implementing file-lock-based leader election with lease management. Leader refreshes lease on each proxy poll; lease expiry triggers re-election.
2. **Coordination file module** — New file (`coordination.ts`) managing the shared coordination JSON file. Each instance reads/writes its entry; entries contain instanceId, workItemId, worklog directory, and timestamps.
3. **Refactored dispatch worker** — Leader-only dispatch logic reads the coordination file, applies tier priority, checks LLM idle, dispatches the highest-priority item, and removes it. Non-leader instances skip proxy polling and dispatch; they only update their coordination entry on the 30-minute check-in.
4. **Updated scheduler** — Non-leader instances use a 30-minute check-in timer for coordination updates; the leader uses the existing proxy-poll cadence (30s) for LLM idle checks plus coordination updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — NEW: File-lock leader election with lease management (TTL, expiry detection, re-election).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — NEW: Shared coordination file read/write (flock, JSON format, entry management).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Refactored: leader checks before dispatch, coordination file integration, tier priority from list.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — May need minor updates to record coordination-file operations alongside dispatches.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Updated: scheduler wiring for leader vs. non-leader timers.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — May need updates for the 30-minute check-in cadence on non-leader instances.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Wire coordination file path and leader election into `createDowntimeDeps`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6** — Downtime dispatcher: priority-first selection with round-robin tie-break (open) — this refactoring **supersedes** the round-robin/jitter approach; that work item should be closed or marked absorbed. This relationship should be recorded as a blocker/absorbed link.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed) — CAS/claim infrastructure this builds on.
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — Log herdr downtime dispatches (completed) — dispatch log pattern reused.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Each instance operates on its own worklog directory, so "most important item" is computed independently per instance using the standard tier priority.
- **Assumption:** The coordination file is stored in a shared `.worklog/` directory accessible to all instances (local filesystem, not network storage in v1).
- **Risk:** Race conditions during coordination file writes (two instances updating simultaneously). Mitigation: flock on write; brief lock-hold (read-modify-write is fast JSON manipulation).
- **Risk:** Leader election race when multiple instances start simultaneously. Mitigation: file lock is atomic; one wins, others detect lock held and retry after a short backoff (e.g., 1-2 seconds).
- **Risk:** Stale entries from crashed instances linger in the coordination file until they expire or are cleaned up. Mitigation: include `lastUpdated` timestamp per entry; the leader can prune entries older than the lease timeout (5 min) on each dispatch cycle.
- **Risk:** Instance's worklog becomes inaccessible during a check-in (disk error, permission change). Mitigation: fail-open — skip the check-in for that instance, do not remove the entry, log the error.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Ensure the refactoring doesn't inadvertently break existing dispatch guard mechanisms (CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion). Extra opportunities (e.g., cross-machine support) are recorded as linked work items, not scope.
- **Risk:** 5-minute lease means up to 5 minutes of no dispatch if leader crashes. Acceptable for v1; could be reduced in a follow-up.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Leader election mechanism?" — Answer (user): "(a) Simple: first to acquire a file lock wins". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Coordination file contents?" — Answer (user): "work item ID and the directory in which the .worklog folder can be found". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Leader failure / handoff?" — Answer (user): "(b) Lease-based: leader gets a time-limited lease and must re-acquire it periodically". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Multi-tier scheduling on leader?" — Answer (user): "if an audit tier work item exists, use that; if not check for an implement item; if none try a plan etc." Source: interactive reply.
- Q5: "LLM idle checking?" — Answer (user): "(a) Leader still checks LLM idle status before dispatching (current behavior)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q6: "Multi-machine support?" — Answer (user): "not supported in first version; flock is OK". Source: interactive reply.
- Q7: "Lease duration?" — Answer (user): "5 minutes, refreshed every time the leader polls the proxy". Source: interactive reply.
- Q8: "Re-queueing after dispatch?" — Answer (user): "yes — when leader dispatches and removes an item, the instance adds its next most important item at the next 30-minute check-in". Source: interactive reply.
- Q9: "Dispatch cadence?" — Answer (user): "same as current: poll proxy every 30s, require ~4 min continuous idle, then dispatch one item and wait for a fresh idle period". Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

## Summary
New `coordination.ts` managing the shared coordination JSON file at `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` with per-instance entry management.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Each instance reads/writes its own entry using flock for safe concurrent access

# Intake Brief: Dispatching continues while downtime dispatch is disabled

**Work item:** WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE · **Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical (operator-specified)
**Date:** 2026-08-22

## Problem statement

The operator disables downtime dispatch via the `d` shortcut (header shows
`[Downtime Off]` on the pane) yet pi agent work continues to be dispatched —
audits, plans and implementations keep spawning, and the ContextHub audit
`WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` was dispatched at 11:05:23Z while the operator believed
dispatch was disabled. The same herdr worklist header later reported
`[⏳ downtime idle 40+ min]` — the enabled-and-idle worker state — in a
session the operator considers disabled. The disable control is not
effective, not durable, or not scoped the way the operator believes.

## Users

- **Herdr operators (multi-workspace)**: disable downtime dispatch to stop
  autonomous work (e.g. while working interactively), and expect that disable
  to hold — without needing to also stop every sibling pane or remember
  in-memory semantics.
  - As an operator I press `d`, see `[Downtime Off]`, and **no** new pi agent
    panes spawn anywhere for that worklog root until I re-enable dispatch.
  - As an operator I can tell, at a glance, which pane(s) are disabled and
    which are still dispatching.

## Acceptance Criteria (initial; refine at plan)

1. **Disabled ⇒ no dispatch, durably.** After one `d` press (header shows
   `[Downtime Off]`), with no further key presses and no manual settings edit,
   the worklist's downtime worker performs no proxy polling, no idle
   tracking, and no dispatch **for at least 60 minutes** (i.e. well past the
   4-minute idle threshold and any 60-minute no-candidate cooldown window).
   Verified by a test that toggles the worker off, advances simulated time
   through the threshold/cooldown boundaries, and asserts zero
   `dispatchDowntimeWork` invocations and zero pane spawns.
2. **No silent re-enable.** If the per-instance override can be lost by any
   real pane/plugin lifecycle event (restart, reload, re-attach), the
   operator must be told explicitly (header/status must not silently return
   to `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` in a pane previously shown `[Downtime Off]`).
   The chosen fix must make the disable state either (a) durable across those
   events, or (b) visibly non-durable with an explicit notice — never a
   silent revert.
3. **Toggle cycle cannot force-enable.** Pressing `d` twice must never leave
   dispatch force-enabled (`override === true`) while the operator believes
   they disabled it: the second press returns to "follow settings" (`null`),
   or re-enable requires explicit confirmation. A test pins the full cycle
   `null → false → null` (or `null → false → (confirmed) true` — decided at
   plan) and asserts `enabled` after each step.
4. **Header honesty.** `renderDowntimeStatus` must never render
   `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` (an enabled, polling worker) in a pane whose
   dispatch gate the operator disabled: the rendered state must always agree
   with the effective dispatch decision of `tick()`. Test: render off /
   enabled / paused / dispatching states against the worker's effective
   enabled state.
5. **Per-pane scope is visible & documented.** The per-instance scope of the
   `d` toggle is preserved (sibling panes unaffected), but the README/help
   makes the scope explicit ("current pane only, in-memory, resets on
   restart"), and each pane's header state (`[Downtime Off]` vs live status)
   lets the operator tell which pane is disabled. Docs updated; acceptance: a
   user reading the README cannot reasonably believe `d` disables dispatch
   for all panes or persists across restarts.
6. **Root-cause regression evidence.** The reproducing evidence for the
   reported incident — ContextHub audit `WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` dispatched
   2026-08-22T11:05:23Z while dispatch was believed disabled, and the
   subsequent 11:05–11:47Z multi-root dispatch wave — is explained by the
   confirmed root cause in a comment/AC write-up, with the confirmation
   steps used (dispatch-log, herdr pane-spawn log, header state).
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (including the
   existing downtime-worker / toggle test suites
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`).

## Constraints

- The per-instance in-memory toggle design (WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF AC2) may be
  changed ONLY where needed to satisfy AC2/AC3; settings file writes and
  cross-pane coupling need explicit operator sign-off at plan.
- Existing dispatch guarantees must not regress: code-freeze gate, dispatched
  marker exclusion, per-tier free-slot minimums, single-flight, no-candidate
  cooldown (see RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT and
  `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`).
- No new dispatch side channels: the fix must not add or remove a dispatch
  mechanism; it only changes when the existing worker dispatches.

## Existing state

- The `d` shortcut (shortcuts.json) → `/downtime toggle` →
  `onDowntimeToggle()` → `downtimeWorker.toggle()` (index.ts:1000-1046,
  worklist.ts:3346-3352).
- `toggle()` cycles the in-memory override `null → false → true → null`
  (downtime-worker.ts:1639-1641): **a second press force-enables dispatch
  (override = true)**, which also overrides a settings-level disable.
- `tick()` short-circuits when `!(override ?? cfg.enabled)`
  (downtime-worker.ts:1658-1661) — the gate is correct for a single worker
  instance.
- `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:2771-2799) renders either
  `[Downtime Off]` (disabled) or `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`
  (enabled + polling): mutually exclusive for one pane.
- The toggle is **in-memory and per-instance**: plugin/pane restart resets
  `override` to `null` (follows settings) with no notice; sibling panes are
  unaffected. Leader-only dispatch (WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5) is blocked, so
  multiple panes dispatch concurrently.
- Observed evidence 2026-08-22 (report incident):
  - ContextHub `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`: audit
    `WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU` dispatched 11:05:23Z (cwd ContextHub); last entry
    for this root.
  - herdr-server.log: four dispatch panes spawned simultaneously 11:05:09–
    11:05:23Z across SorraAgents / open_source_llm / Tableau-Card-Engine /
    ContextHub (pids 302077/302156/302252/302464); further panes 11:12Z,
    11:15Z, 11:42Z, 11:47Z (sibling roots only).
  - No worklist-pane (plugin) restart is evident in herdr-server.log between
    the incident and the report; the `/downtime toggle` press itself is not
    recorded in worklog-command-log.json (internal action, unlogged).
  - Config `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` has no `downtimeEnabled`
    key → all workers enabled by default.

## Desired change

Downtime dispatch, once disabled, must actually stop dispatching for the
worklog root the operator is controlling and stay stopped until explicitly
re-enabled — with the header state always agreeing with the effective gate,
and with the per-pane/in-memory scope either made durable or made explicit.
Root-cause confirmation at implementation must decide between (ranked):

- **H1 — override lost/cycled after the press:** pane/plugin lifecycle or a
  second `d` press reverted the override (`null` → settings-enabled, or
  `false` → `true` force-on). Explains the audit dispatch at 11:05:23Z and
  the later idle-40+min header. Validation: reproduce toggle → restart /
  second press → assert dispatch resumes silently (AC2/AC3).
- **H2 — in-flight dispatch completed after the press:** a dispatch already
  running when `d` was pressed completed (single-flight; marker written after
  spawn). Explains one late dispatch, not the continued idle reporting.
  Validation: press `d` while `dispatching === true`; assert the in-flight
  dispatch still logs (acceptable) but no NEW dispatch starts (AC1).
- **H3 — scope mismatch:** the observed dispatch came from another enabled
  pane (sibling workspace/root) while the toggled pane was correctly off.
  Explains continuing sibling-root dispatches and an idle header in an
  untoggled pane. Validation: enumerate panes/workspaces, reproduce
  per-instance toggle (AC5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `toggle()` cycle (~1639),
  `tick()` gate (~1658), `createDowntimeWorker` override lifecycle; where
  durable-override and cycle fixes land.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `renderDowntimeStatus` (~2771),
  `/downtime toggle` routing (3346), scheduler task registration (5066);
  header-honesty fix, persisted-state notice, README-adjacent help hints.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — worker wiring + `onDowntimeToggle`
  (~1000-1046); sole `createDowntimeWorker` call site.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings` schema (43-79);
  durable override key if persistence is chosen (constraint: needs sign-off).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `d` → `/downtime toggle` (line 4).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — scope/durability documentation (AC5).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`.
- Evidence: `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`,
  `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log`,
  `~/.config/herdr/worklog-command-log.json`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — Shortcut key to toggle downtime dispatch per
  herdr instance (parent design; in_review). AC2 mandates in-memory
  per-instance; AC4 mandates the tick short-circuit. This bug is the first
  real-world failure of that design's durability/scope expectations.
- **WL-0MSZS1NNV0075NFI** — Header rendering `[Downtime Off]` (completed).
- **WL-0MSZS1OHV0067JD1** — README docs for `d` / `[Downtime Off]`
  (completed; docs now need the scope/durability caveat).
- **WL-0MSXHA1B0005G3E5** — Leader-only dispatch logic (blocked): while
  unimplemented, multiple panes dispatch concurrently, amplifying any
  per-pane disable gap.
- **WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66** — Active-audit single-flight tests (open): audit
  dispatch multiplicity guard, adjacent to the reported multi-dispatch wave.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — Prior downtime dispatch
  duplication RCA + fix (completed): dispatch-path guarantees this fix must
  not regress.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-config-audit-2026-08-08.md`,
  `packages/herdr/docs/downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — single root cause may not exist:** the evidence is
  consistent with H1+H3 jointly (override lost AND sibling panes dispatching
  regardless). ACs are written against the observable contract so the fix
  covers the failure class, not one mechanism.
- **Risk — persistence changes settings semantics:** making the override
  durable (e.g. writing a per-project marker) touches the shared settings /
  marker files and could affect multi-pane behavior; needs operator sign-off
  at plan (constraint).
- **Risk — scope creep:** attractive extras (global kill switch, per-project
  master disable, leader-only completion) are adjacent but out of scope;
  file as follow-ups, do not fold in.
- **Mitigation — evidence kit preserved:** dispatch log, herdr pane-spawn
  log excerpts and header-state observations are recorded above and in work
  item comments so the implementer can verify the confirmed root cause
  without guessing.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How did you disable dispatching? (a) pressed `d` → header showed
  `[Downtime Off]` on the pane you were looking at; (b) set `downtimeEnabled:
  false` in the herdr config; (c) something else?" — Answer (operator,
  interactive): **(a)** pressed `d`, header showed `[Downtime Off]`.
- Q2: "Where does the 'idle 40+ minutes' report appear?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **the herdr worklist header
  (`[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`)**.
- Q3: "Which audit dispatch violated your disable intent?" — Answer
  (operator, interactive): **`WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU`** (ContextHub root;
  dispatched 2026-08-22T11:05:23Z per dispatch log; pane spawned
  11:05:23.495Z per herdr-server.log).
- OPEN QUESTION 1: Was `d` pressed exactly once in the flagged pane, or more
  than once? (Discriminates H1-cycle from H1-restart / H3.)
- OPEN QUESTION 2: Which workspace/tab displayed `[Downtime Off]` vs the
  header showing `[⏳ downtime idle 40+ min]` — the same pane or different
  panes? (Discriminates H3.)
- OPEN QUESTION 3: Was the flagged worklist pane restarted/re-attached
  between the `d` press and the observed dispatch? (herdr-server.log shows no
  plugin-pane respawn in the window, but herdr may not log all lifecycle
  events.)

- `CLI.md` — matched: audit, bug, continues, disabled, extension (+9 more)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Rendered state agrees with effective gate.** For each effective state (off/override=false, enabled+idle, enabled+paused, dispatching), renderDowntimeStatus output is asserted against the worker's effective enabled state. A pane whose dispatch gate is disabled (override false) NEVER renders the enabled-idle string `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`.
2. **Disabled renders [Downtime Off].** worker.override === false renders `[Downtime Off]` regardless of global settings.enabled.
3. **Enabled renders live status.** worker.override === null with settings enabled and idleSince set renders the idle string; dispatching renders the dispatching string; paused renders the paused string.

5. **After re-enable, notice is gone.** When override returns to null AND the marker file is absent, no notice renders (back to normal live status).
6. **Existing header tests pass.** No regression in worklist.test.ts header render tests.
